reason: A keeps the dark brand panel, but the sun icon and SOLSTICE wordmark are jammed against its edges and the panel looks cropped. The eyebrow is stranded under the panel, 'Ships late June' is squeezed into a three-line sliver, and the legal text is microscopic, roughly as prominent as the body. B drops the dark band, so the white SOLSTICE logo sits nearly invisible on cream, which is a brand failure. B also cuts the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow loose to the far right, away from the headline it introduces, and the CTA is small and crammed under the body copy next to tiny legal text.

A: the 'Reserve a Case' CTA has shrunk to an unreadable chip on the right and the oversized body copy outranks it, so the hierarchy is inverted. The 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is gone and the legal and 'Ships late June' text are illegibly small. B: the CTA is a readable button and the eyebrow survives, but the orange divider strikes through 'Golden Evenings' in the last headline line. The Solstice logo is tiny and overpowered by the eyebrow, and the legal text is cramped and unreadable. Its hierarchy is still more usable than A's.

A: the dark header is now a dead block in the top-left with the logo shrunk to an unreadable speck, the orange divider floats alone, the body copy and 'Ships late June' are bigger than the tiny 'Reserve a Case' button, and the legal text is crammed into the bottom-right corner, so the brand is effectively lost and the hierarchy is inverted. B: the logo is far too large and competes with the headline, the dark bar is a stray fragment at the top right, the divider floats, the body copy is squeezed into a narrow ragged column placed above the CTA but away from the headline, and 'Ships late June' wraps awkwardly next to illegible legal text. Still, B keeps the brand mark intact and the headline dominant, so it is the less bad resize.

A: the logo bar has shrunk to an inset white box with uneven margins, and the headline sits right under it with no gap. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow has moved to the bottom-left at a tiny, unreadable size, and the divider almost touches the headline; the CTA is still large, centred and prominent. B: the full-width logo band and the eyebrow keep their original look, but the divider now sits between the eyebrow and the headline, and the top half has a lot of dead space while the bottom is cramped. The body copy is tiny, and the CTA is small, left-aligned against the centred layout and pinned near the bottom edge, which buries the call to action.

A is the original column shrunk into the middle of the 320×50 banner. The headline, body and CTA are microscopic and unreadable, the white logo bar is a sliver, and about 80% of the canvas is empty navy. B at least uses the banner format, reading left to right with body copy, then headline, then the 'Reserve a Case' button. But the logo and the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow are gone, and the left body copy and 'Ships late June' are too small to read. The headline is jammed into three cramped lines with almost no margin, and the CTA is pressed against the right edge.

A drops the Solstice logo and dark brand band. The headline wraps to three lines on the left. The body copy is stretched into one long line too small to read, and the tiny CTA sits jammed under it, so the button is buried. B keeps the logo and dark strip on the left and groups the headline with the CTA in the centre, which gives a clearer focal point. But its wrapped body copy is nearly as heavy as the headline and competes with it, the legal block is illegible, and the eyebrow is lost in both.

A: the oversized headline takes up half the banner, and the right half is a jumble. The CTA, badges and tilted FREE DELIVERY pill are scattered in a 2x2 cluster with no grid, and the body copy is squeezed into a narrow ragged column against the right edge. The product circle is also cropped at the top. B: a cleaner left-to-right banner with the product on the left and the text stacked beside it, but GROVE now sits below the headline and is oversized, which reverses the brand order. The CTA has shrunk to the same weight as the badges in one cramped row, and the tilted FREE DELIVERY pill is wedged between them; the shoe's sole also runs past the left side of its circle.

A: the 'NEW' badge and the 'Try It' button both sit on top of the shrunken product circle, so three elements collide in one cramped middle cluster. The subcopy is pushed to the far right as a narrow three-line ragged block, which breaks the reading order (headline, then badge/product/CTA, then copy), and the headline wraps awkwardly onto two lines. B: it keeps the original left-to-right structure, clear hierarchy and brand colours, but it is essentially a straight shrink. The subcopy and the 'NEW' pill text are around 5px and barely legible, the product circle is cropped at the top and left edges, and there is dead space between the copy and the badge.

A: the quote is squeezed into a narrow 5-line column that starts almost at the top edge. The quote mark is moved to mid-height beside the text instead of leading it, and the logo floats centred under the attribution, off the text's left edge. B: it keeps the original's left-column order (quote mark, quote, attribution) with a readable 3-line quote, but the attribution breaks onto two lines and the logo sits beside it as a competing element. The glass also rides high in its circle, leaving an empty lower half.

A: the can is shrunk to a small, off-centre object inside a circle that drifts left, so its 'SOLSTICE' label is unreadable. The logo sits jammed under the attribution, and there are dead bands of space above the quote and below the circle. B: the can is larger and its label is legible, which makes it a proper focal point. Its flaws: the circle bleeds off the right edge and sits off-centre from the can, the logo is still crammed tight under the attribution, and the gap between the quote mark and the quote is large.

A: the SAVE 15% badge is oversized, cut off at the left edge and outweighs the headline; the coffee bag is shrunk to a speck next to a tiny logo under the CTA; the right third is an empty blurred brown block; and the body copy is cramped right under the headline. B reads left to right with a clear headline, a visible product bag and a CTA in its own space, but the logo badge is too big and competes with the headline, the bag is small, the body copy is small, and the SAVE badge floats loose on the left.

A: a clean left-to-right banner with a big headline and a large, clear CTA. But the '48H ONLY' badge has shrunk until it can't be read, the box is crowded into the bottom-left corner, and the lime panel now bleeds off the edge, so the original's framed card is gone. B keeps the framed lime card, which is more faithful, but it has the same unreadable badge, the box is jammed against the bottom edge, and the body copy and CTA are squeezed into a small right column. That leaves the CTA weak and dead space to the left of the headline.

A breaks the hero graphic: the shoe has slid off its lime circle, which now sits clipped low-right as a stray blob. The NEW VIDEO badge sits awkwardly to the left of the logo on a different baseline, and the headline wraps to leave 'marathons' alone on its own line. B keeps the shoe inside its circle and puts logo and badge in a clean top row with a strong two-line headline, but the shoe circle is shrunk into the lower-left, 'Full review inside.' floats apart from everything, and the bottom third feels thin and empty.

A keeps the confetti backdrop and the book cover beside the card, so it still reads as the same design. But the logo is shrunk to an illegible speck and crammed into a corner beside the eyebrow, the card bleeds off the top and right edges, and the legal copy is set nearly as large as the body text next to the CTA. B drops the confetti background entirely and turns the canvas into a flat cream panel, losing the brand's signature texture. Its body copy is about as big as the headline and competes with it, and the book cover is jammed into the top-left corner while the logo floats on its own, which makes the layout feel scattered.

A keeps the clean left-aligned quote column with good margins, but the quote mark is stranded far above the quote with a dead gap between them, the logo floats in the middle of the attribution row instead of on a clear edge, and the glass sits high and off-centre in its circle. B crams the oversized quote against the top edge in five choppy lines, moves the opening quote mark to the side, halfway down the text block, which looks odd, and centres the logo under left-aligned text so nothing lines up, though the glass sits well inside its circle.

A does rearrange the design into a left-to-right banner (headline left, body middle, Reserve a Case CTA right), but the Q logo and dark header band are gone. Its body copy and legal line are microscopic and unreadable, the 'Ships late June' line is jammed above the CTA, and the long headline is crammed into six tiny lines. B just shrinks the portrait original into a narrow centred column with huge empty bands on both sides, so every piece of text, the logo and the CTA are illegible specks. That is a squashed copy, not a resize, and is unusable.

A: reads left to right and has a proper-sized CTA, but the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow and its stray divider sit stranded under the logo block, far from the headline. The three-line headline is jammed between the columns with almost no gutter, and the legal text crowds right under the CTA. B: the CTA is a tiny pill buried at the bottom right next to legal text of almost the same width, so it is the weakest element. The body copy is set so large that it competes with the headline, the headline hugs the bottom edge, and a stray divider line floats in the corner.

A shifts the whole layout down evenly to fill the slightly taller canvas. The can stays nested inside its circle, the text column lines up with the circle's centre, and the spacing matches the original. B leaves the circle where it was but moves the can down, so the can's lower corners now poke past the circle's edge and the illustration loses its centred lockup. B's text block also stretches lower than the circle's centre, with a looser gap above the pills and button, so the two halves feel out of balance.

A actually rearranges the design for the taller canvas: the headline sits on top and the bottle is large. But the headline floats off-axis with dead space to its right, the NEW pill drifts alone between the bottle and the CTA, and the decorative circle is cropped into the top-left corner. B is just the original leaderboard strip pasted into the middle, with large empty orange bands above and below, a tiny bottle, the decorative circle clashing with the bottle's circle, and the Try It button jammed against the right edge.

A scatters its elements with no grouping: the headline sits alone at top-left, the subline is stranded at the bottom-right far from it, the ONLINE ONLY badge floats in empty space, Try It sits in the right column away from its copy, and the headline is undersized for the canvas. B has a reasonable top-to-bottom order (phone, headline, subline, badge, CTA), but the cream circle that sat behind the phone has come loose and is clipped in the bottom-left corner. B's text is left-aligned while the badge and CTA are centred, the headline is small, and there is dead space at the top, so it is the less broken of the two.

A: the cream circle that sat behind the phone has come loose and sits as a stray blob cut off at the bottom-left corner. The 'ONLINE ONLY' badge floats alone at the top left. The headline and subcopy are left-aligned while the phone and CTA are centred, so nothing shares an axis, and there are big empty gaps between the blocks. B: the phone still sits on its circle, so it is closer to the original. But the headline is small and stuck at the top left, the badge floats alone in the middle right, and the subcopy has fallen to the bottom right under the CTA. That breaks the reading order and leaves large dead areas on the right side.

A: the attribution 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' sits in the middle of the canvas, away from the quote it belongs to, and floats above an oversized SOLSTICE logo. The quote is squeezed into a narrow four-line column at the left edge, and the product inside its circle is small, which leaves dead space. B: the quote and attribution stay together as one readable block, and the product reads well. However, the quote mark is so large it competes with the headline, the quote is cramped against the top edge, and the logo floats under the attribution without sharing its left edge.

Both use the same left text block: quote mark, headline, attribution. In both, the brand logo floats in the middle of the banner, cut off from the other elements. A shrinks the can to a tiny icon in the middle of a full circle, so the SOLSTICE label can't be read and the product is trivial. B keeps the can much larger with the circle bleeding off the edge like the original, so the product holds up better, though its label is still very small and the can sits close to the bottom edge.

A: clean left-to-right banner with the quote on a tidy 3-line stack and the product centred in its circle, but the SOLSTICE logo floats alone in the middle gap with no alignment to anything, and the attribution is almost as loud as the quote. B: the 2-line quote reads well, but the logo is jammed beside the attribution and against the product circle, and the product is shrunk and pushed to the top of its circle so its label is illegible. That makes the right side look cramped and arbitrary.

Both are nearly identical 320x50 strips. In both, the hierarchy is inverted: the orange 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' attribution is set bolder and louder than the quote, which is crammed into three tiny serif lines that are barely readable. In both, the SOLSTICE sun logo is dropped and the product jar shrinks to an illegible speck at the far right. A keeps the maroon circle behind the jar, so it stays slightly closer to the original. B's jar has lost its backdrop and looks like a stray orange block.

A: the purple circle is cut off in the top-right corner and no longer sits behind the can, so it reads as a random blob and the product loses its backdrop. The attribution 'THE ULTRA TASTING TEAM' sits above the quote, which reverses the original reading order, though the quote is large and readable. B: it keeps the can on its circle, but the can is small, the quote mark is oversized with a dead gap below it, the attribution is also above the quote, and the logo row floats mid-canvas between the quote and the product instead of anchoring the bottom.

A: the can is a strong hero and the quote column reads well, but the attribution is enlarged to nearly headline weight and competes with the quote. The circle is clipped at the top edge, the logo is moved off its corner into the circle under the can, and there is a large dead gap between the quote mark and the text. B: the circle is fully contained, but the smaller can floats in the top of the circle over a big empty lower half. The logo is jammed onto the attribution line like a stray fragment, and the quote leaves a short 'too soon.' last line.

A makes the lime panel full-bleed, which loses the original's inset card on stripes. The product box sits right on the panel's top edge with no gap, the 48H badge is oversized and fights the headline, and the CTA is jammed close to the bottom. B keeps the inset lime card framed by stripes and leaves a clear gap between box and panel, so it is truer to the original. Its flaws: the badge is crowded against the box, the headline almost fills the narrow card's width with thin side margins, and the CTA sits tight to the card's bottom edge.

A keeps the Inkwell & Lantern logo legible and the headline dominant, but the card bleeds off the top, bottom and right edges, and the '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' eyebrow is cut off from the headline and parked under the logo. The legal text beside the CTA is also microscopic. B keeps the eyebrow above the headline and the floating card over confetti, which is truer to the original, but the logo is shrunk to an illegible speck in the corner, a brand failure. Its CTA is also small and cramped next to tiny legal text.

A has a clean three-column banner with a clear headline and CTA, but it drops 'The Quiet Hours' book cover, which is the key image, and shrinks the Inkwell & Lantern logo to an unreadable speck in the corner; the fine print is also tiny. B keeps the book, but the card runs off the canvas edges, and the logo sits on top of busy confetti right against the left edge. B's eyebrow line '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' is moved below the book, breaks into an awkward two-line wrap and is as big as the body copy, which muddles the reading order and the hierarchy.

A just shrinks the portrait design into a narrow centre strip of the wide banner: the headline, body and CTA are microscopic and illegible, and huge empty cream areas fill both sides, so it is a shrunk copy, not a resize. B properly re-flows the ad left to right (headline block left, body copy centre, Reserve a Case CTA right), but the dark header bar and Q logo are missing or lost, the 6-line headline is cramped against the left edge, the body copy is tiny, and 'Ships late June' and the legal line are near-illegible fragments.

A: the quote, attribution and logo sit together in one left block and read left to right, but the logo is now about as big as the attribution and floats centred under it, off the text's left edge. The huge quote mark crowds the copy, and the attribution is oversized next to the quote. B: the attribution is cut off from its quote and floats mid-canvas in tiny, hard-to-read type. The quote is jammed into the bottom-left with an orphaned quote mark far above it, the logo is oversized in the centre, and the right-hand circle and can are small and leave dead space, so the layout looks scattered.

Both use the same decent left-to-right banner structure: the quote mark and headline sit together on the left with the attribution under them. Both have the same flaw: the brand logo floats in the middle gap with no alignment to anything and reads like stray debris. A's can is larger and fills its circle, so the product and its SOLSTICE label stay legible, though the sun icon is jammed against the circle's top edge. B shrinks the can to a tiny figure inside a big empty circle, which makes the label unreadable and weakens the product.

A keeps the original structure: a lime card framed by the stripes, with badge, box, headline, body and CTA in a clean vertical order. Its flaws are small: the badge crowds the top of the box, the margins at the card's bottom edge are tight, and the box is quite small. B turns the lime card into a full-bleed block, so the framed-card look is lost. The box sits awkwardly across the stripe/lime seam, the 48H badge is oversized and competes with the headline, and the CTA is jammed against the canvas's bottom edge.

A: the logo is legible on the left and the headline reads well, but the dark header band is left as a stray black slab in the top-right corner, a lone orange rule floats at top-left, and the 'Reserve a Case' CTA and legal text are tiny, so the CTA is buried. B: a huge dark block takes up the left quarter with the logo shrunk to an illegible dot inside it, the orange rule is stranded below it, and the CTA and legal text are just as tiny, which wrecks both the brand and the hierarchy.

A shrinks the Q logo to an illegible speck at the bottom corner of a large empty dark block, so the brand mark is effectively lost and the panel reads as dead space. B keeps the logo large and legible in the dark panel, but its orange divider cuts through the 'Rosemary' line of the headline. Both cram the body copy, CTA and legal into the bottom strip with tiny text and a small button.

A drops the white logo panel, so the dark logo sits almost invisibly on navy. Its 'Ships late June' note is crushed into an illegible sliver beside the CTA, and the body copy is jammed against the right edge, leaving the left third mostly empty except for a tiny eyebrow. B keeps the logo on its white panel with the eyebrow underneath, and groups the CTA with its ship note, so it reads cleanly left to right. B still needs work: the four-line headline is dense, the body copy is too small to read at banner size, and the CTA is pressed close to the top edge.

A: the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow has moved below the headline and shrunk until it can't be read, the orange divider rule is stranded at the very bottom under the legal copy, and the legal text is almost as large as the body copy. B has the same eyebrow and legal-text problems, and its header band is squeezed thin, so the logo is tiny and the sun mark is barely visible or lost. B's divider sits more sensibly above the headline, but A keeps the logo more intact, so A is marginally better.

Both use the same flawed structure: the CTA sits at the top of the right column above the badges, which breaks the reading order, and the body copy is pushed into the bottom-right corner, away from the headline. A keeps the product inside its circle as in the original, and its headline sets cleanly in two lines. B breaks the headline into three lines, leaving 'back' as an orphan, and shrinks the circle so the shoe spills past it on the left; its body copy is also crammed against the bottom edge.

A has a sound top-to-bottom story stack (brand, headline, large hero circle). But the CTA 'Find It Near You' has shrunk to a tiny pill the same size as the badges, so it is buried in a row of four, and body copy now sits below the CTA, which breaks the reading order. B is broken: the hero product is shrunk into the top-right corner, the headline floats mid-left beside scattered pills, and there are large dead gaps. The CTA is tiny, badges and body copy are strewn down the right column, and the layout has no grid or grouping.

A keeps the phone-and-circle hero and a strong headline, but the CTA is shrunk to badge size and crammed into a bottom row with the tagline, which wraps awkwardly ('Cool, crisp / and barely / sweet.'); the 3-line headline also overpowers everything. B shrinks the phone hero to a tiny icon jammed into the bottom-left corner with its circle almost gone, makes the badges as big as the CTA (no hierarchy), and leaves 'SOLSTICE' tiny and squeezed beside the headline, so the key imagery is lost.

A: the phone has shrunk to a small mid-canvas object, leaving big dead gaps above and below it. The left-aligned headline clashes with the centred SOLSTICE wordmark, the subline is tiny, and the two badges now sit stacked below the CTA, so the reading order is reversed and the CTA gets buried mid-stack. B: it keeps the same flaws (left-aligned headline under a centred wordmark, tiny subline, badges after the CTA and jammed near the bottom edge), and the green circle is cropped into odd slivers at both canvas edges. Even so, its larger phone fills the column, the spacing is tighter and the hero has real presence, so it reads as more deliberate than A's half-empty stack.

A: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow has been moved below the subhead, which breaks the original reading order, and the headline runs into the circle. There's also a large dead gap between the shoe and the CTA, and the legal text is very small. Still, the structure is clean and the CTA is clear. B: keeps the eyebrow order, but the shoe sits off-centre at the bottom-left edge of the circle instead of on it. The subhead 'Every mixed case.' is squeezed into three ragged one-word lines next to the button, and the legal text is crammed under the CTA, so the bottom is cramped while the circle area above it is mostly empty.

A: the bottle-in-circle shrinks to a tiny icon jammed against the top edge and stacked on top of the Try It button, so the product is lost. NEW and Try It are small and crowded into the right corner. B: the bottle is a readable size, but it has lost its circle backdrop, is clipped at the bottom edge and sits tight against the headline. The NEW badge also overlaps the top of the Try It button and pushes against the top edge. B is marginally better because the product stays visible.

A keeps the bottle-in-cream-circle composition. But the 'Blood Orange Sunset' headline is a tiny line in the top-left corner, NEW and Try It are small and pushed apart along the bottom edge (NEW hard left, CTA off-centre), there is a big dead orange band, and a faint stray circle fragment sits in the top-left corner. B centres NEW and Try It under the bottle, which groups them better. However, it pulls the cream circle away from the bottle and dumps it as a clipped blob in the bottom-left corner, adds the same stray top-left fragment, leaves the headline tiny and left-aligned against a centred column, and makes the CTA undersized. That broken circle is the more visible defect.

A: the headline 'Blood Orange Sunset' runs straight into the phone's cream circle. The subline is split away from the headline and dropped under the CTA on the right, so headline, product and supporting copy no longer form a group and the reading order is broken. B: it keeps the original's grouping, order and brand intact with no collisions. But it is barely more than the original banner stretched wider and centred: the content sits in a thin middle strip with large empty orange bands above and below, the text and phone are small for the taller canvas, and the cream circle is cropped hard at the left edge.

A reads left to right: the quote wraps over three lines, then the can on its maroon circle, then the yellow attribution, which stays legible. But the SOLSTICE logo is gone, the can is tiny with an unreadable label, and the circle is cramped against the top and bottom edges. B drops the attribution completely, and its sun logo and SOLSTICE wordmark are shrunk to an illegible speck floating in a dead middle gap. That leaves the can isolated at the far right and the banner looking empty and unbalanced.

A keeps the circle behind the product, but it moves the attribution above the quote, which breaks the reading order. Its SOLSTICE logo is also shrunk to an almost unreadable speck, squeezed between the quote and the product. B cuts the circle off at the top right, where it floats behind the quote mark and no longer sits behind the can, so the original's look is lost. B also drops the attribution to the bottom edge as tiny fine print far from its quote, and its logo is a cramped, unreadable speck right under the text.

A: the attribution 'THE ULTRA TASTING TEAM' is shrunk to tiny, barely readable text, while the logo is blown up far beyond its original size and sits on the same line as the attribution, so it outweighs it. The can is also small inside a big, mostly empty circle. B: the attribution stays readable and the logo sits under the product, which groups them sensibly. Its flaws are a 5-line quote with awkward breaks ('a / little bitter,'), a logo that is still oversized, and a circle pushed into the top-right corner and cropped, which leaves dead space below it on the right.

A: the product photo is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail the same size as the logo, so the two compete side by side, and a large dead gap separates them from the body copy; the headline also breaks into a weak 'on' line. B: the bag is cut out at a more readable size but again sits next to an equal-weight logo, and the leftover blurred background photo has become a large, empty brown rectangle between the copy and the CTA. That block looks like a rendering error and wastes a third of the canvas, so A is only slightly less broken.

A reads cleanly as a banner: striped panel with the badge and the shoebox on the left, then the headline with the body copy under it, and the CTA on the far right. The headline leads clearly. Its flaws are small: the body line is tiny at 90px tall, and the badge sits close to the box. B clips the pink '48H ONLY' badge against the left canvas edge. The shoebox straddles the stripe/lime boundary awkwardly, and the striped panel is squeezed to a sliver. The small body copy sits stacked above the CTA in a cramped right column, so the right side looks crowded while the middle is padded.

A: the headline runs right into the lime circle with almost no gap, the shoe is shrunk to a tiny icon, 'Full review inside.' wraps into a cramped three-line stack against the right edge, and the 'NEW VIDEO' pill text is squished. B: the headline has room to breathe, the shoe stays readable as a deliberate bleed, and the badge and copy stay intact, but 'Full review inside.' is very small and floats on the far right away from the other elements, and the circle is cropped hard at the top and bottom.

Both reverse the reading order: the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow now sits below the headline and is shrunk until you can't read it. In both, 'Small-Batch' runs almost into the canvas edges, and the legal text is nearly as large as the body copy. In A the header band is squashed thin, the SOLSTICE logo is tiny and the sun mark is almost gone, and the orange rule has floated up under the header. B keeps a taller header with a visible sun icon, so the brand survives a bit better, but its orange rule ends up stranded at the very bottom under the legal text and the wordmark is still tiny.

A is scattered: the product is shrunk into the top-right corner, the headline floats mid-left with a big dead gap above it, the tiny CTA sits in a random pill cluster with badges, and the body copy is stranded at bottom-right in a narrow, ragged column. B has a clear top-to-bottom order (brand, headline, large product, then pills, then copy) on a shared left edge, but the CTA has been shrunk to a tiny pill in a row with the badges so it no longer stands out, the body copy ends up last, below the action, and the bottom feels slightly empty.

A squeezes 'Every mixed case.' into a cramped three-line stack beside the CTA, which makes the bottom band crowded, and pushes the legal line into a tiny cramped caption under the button. The shoe also sits awkwardly off-centre against the big empty circle, leaving dead space in the middle. B keeps a clean headline/subcopy/product/CTA sequence with a large, well-scaled shoe, but it moves the 'WEEKEND ONLY' kicker below the subcopy (wrong reading order), mixes a left-aligned text column with a centred CTA, leaves a loose gap above the button, and its legal text is tiny.

A keeps the headline large and readable and the bottle at a usable size, but it drops the cream circle behind the bottle, moves the product from the left lead to the middle-right, and stacks the NEW pill tight against the Try It button with almost no gap. B keeps NEW and Try It side by side like the original, but shrinks the product to a tiny circle jammed into the top-right corner against the canvas edge, so the key image becomes trivial and the right end looks cramped.

A drops the attribution and floats a sun-mark logo in the middle whose SOLSTICE wordmark is too small to read; the small can-and-circle sits off on its own, so the right half is mostly dead space and the layout looks scattered. B fills the banner from left to right (quote, can, attribution) with better balance, but it drops the logo, and the attribution in bold yellow caps is set nearly as large as the quote, so the two compete for attention.

A: the orange divider runs straight through the body copy ('gone'); the body copy is squeezed into a narrow right column that wraps into a tall, ragged stack of 9 lines; the dark header band stops short of the right edge and leaves a cream strip above it; the CTA and legal text are tiny. B: there are no collisions, but the layout is scattered. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow sits at the bottom-left below the headline, the divider floats loose under the logo block, 'Ships late June' is cut off from its CTA and parked above the legal text, the CTA is undersized and the logo is very small. B is the less broken of the two.

A: the dark header band floats under an empty cream strip, the eyebrow is crammed into the header, and the body copy and CTA sit left of the centred headline, so the layout has no shared axis; the gaps around the body are also large and uneven. B: keeps a full-bleed header and a consistent centred axis, but the divider now sits above the eyebrow instead of under the headline, the vertical gaps between headline, body and CTA are oversized and uneven, and the legal line is microscopic.

A: the CTA and 'Back by demand' pill are crammed into the top-right corner, before the copy they should follow; the product sits awkwardly on the GROVE wordmark, 'Summer only' is cut off from its sibling pill, and the body line is illegible at banner size.
